opportunities.title: Coinbase and Bithumb Both Got Breached This Week — And Both Blamed Someone Else
opportunities.why_now: Two major exchanges disclosed breaches on the same day, both pointing to a vendor/internal system rather than their own security, making the 'not us' incident-response playbook impossible to ignore.
opportunities.angle: Pattern analysis: compare both disclosures line by line, show how 'vendor breach' and 'employee system' language functions as liability deflection, and explain what data was actually exposed in each.

opportunities.title: Keystone's Breach Means Someone Can Mail You a Fake Hardware Wallet With Your Real Address On It
opportunities.why_now: A stolen signing key plus leaked buyer addresses turns a data breach into a physical social-engineering vector against hardware wallet owners specifically.
opportunities.angle: Security explainer/checklist: how the key theft enables device spoofing, what Keystone owners should verify before trusting any device or package, and why 'cold storage' isn't breach-proof.

opportunities.title: Datavault AI Can't Withdraw Its Own Bitcoin — That's Not a Hack, It's Worse
opportunities.why_now: A $150M bitcoin treasury deal just froze overnight and the stock halved, a cleaner illustration than most hacks of why counterparty/custody structure matters more than the 'is it hacked' headline.
opportunities.angle: Explainer distinguishing custody failure from a hack: trace the deal structure, who actually controls the keys, and why 'can't access' stories are the quieter, more common version of losing your coins.

opportunities.title: The AI Vulnerability Apocalypse Is On Schedule, Says the Guy Who Runs Bug Bounties for a Living
opportunities.why_now: Immunefi's CEO is flagging AI-generated/AI-found vulnerabilities as a structural shift right as Google previews an AI-threat custody product, giving both sides of the same emerging risk in one news cycle.
opportunities.angle: Two-source feature: pair the Immunefi warning with Google's custody announcement to argue AI is simultaneously the new attacker and the new defense, with concrete predictions for what breaks next.

opportunities.title: $953,000 Drained Faster Than You Can Microwave Popcorn: Inside the Bloom Bot Hack
opportunities.why_now: A sub-two-minute trading-bot exploit is a perfect, visceral case study in how automated systems compress the window for human reaction to zero.
opportunities.angle: Fast technical breakdown: minute-by-minute timeline of the drain, what the bot was trusted to do, and why 'set and forget' trading bots are a growing attack surface worth pricing into risk.
